records.Etymology: 1. Kurkh. ekka ‘tortoise’, Malt. eke ‘a kind of small tortoise’ (Pfeiffer [1972: 185], DEDR 773) — cf. Nancowry ʔok-teka ‘tortoise’ which seems to be a synonym compound where -teka compares with Nyaheun tʌːk ‘tortoise’ and similar MK forms.

records.Gloss: to be under the effect of drink or poison, be intoxicated
records.Etymology: 2. Kurkh. oṅgkhnā/uŋgkhnā (uŋgkhyas) ‘to get drunk, be intoxicated’, Malt. onqe ‘to be under the effect of drink or poison, be intoxicated’ (DEDR 936) — cf. PMK *ʔuək ‘to drink’ but mostly non-alcoholic drinks except Car ʔɔː-kə ‘to be drunk’. Somewhat doubtful.

records.Etymology: 3. Kurkh. cãʔ (Pfeiffer, but Burrow and Emeneau give cāˈ(a)nā [cã̄cas]) ‘to stink, give forth an offensive smell; to smell in general’, Malt. cenye (ceṉca) to emit odour; ceṉyro ‘scented, smelling’ (DEDR 2264) — probably AA, cf. PMK *cʔeh ‘to stink’ and e.g. Kui (ʔa)cēñ ‘stink of urine’.

records.Etymology: 4. Kurkh. teṅgnā (tiṅgyas) ‘to tell, narrate, explain’, Malt. tenge ‘to tell, point out, relate’ (DEDR 3409) — Sre ntiŋ ‘to tell, to charge a commission’, Tampuan tɛɛŋ ‘tell, speak about’ and taiŋ ‘tell, speak about’, Palaung taiŋ ‘to speak’.
